acme_prod: Heads up: our SSE streams from the API keep ending mid-response. The last JSON object is truncated and there's no finish_reason on the final choice — client throws a JSON parse error. Happening ~10% in prod.

sasha_support: Thanks — sorry you hit this. Can you share the exact request you used (curl or SDK), any proxy/edge in front (Fastly/Cloudfront), and a small sample of the truncated payload? /cc @max_engineer :thumbsup:

acme_prod: Node 18 fetch wrapper, SDK v2.1.2. Fastly sits in front of origin. Cropped last chunk we get: 
```json
{"id":"resp_123","choices":[{"text":"...","finish_reason":
```
It literally stops there — client sees unexpected EOF.

sasha_support: Can you run this and paste raw output + response headers? Also include the `x-redwood-trace` header if present.

```bash
curl -i --http1.1 -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```

max_engineer: This smells like proxy buffering / premature close at the edge. Quick checks:
- confirm responses show `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and *no* `Content-Length`
- force HTTP/1.1 (curl --http1.1) to rule out HTTP/2 framing differences
- bypass Fastly/origin directly to see if the stream completes

We've seen Fastly buffer and then send incomplete bodies if the origin closes unexpectedly or if buffering collides with header mutations.

acme_prod: Ran curl --http1.1 --verbose. We see `server: fastly` and on the truncated connections the headers include `Content-Length: 0`. When we hit origin directly (bypass Fastly) the stream completes fine. Repro is consistent through Fastly.

sasha_support: Thanks — escalating to infra. Please attach the raw curl output, response headers, and any pcaps + timestamps. Include the `x-redwood-trace` value from the response if present. I'll open a support ticket so infra can correlate edge+origin logs.

infra_bot: Support ticket SUP-9831 created and assigned to @max_engineer. Please upload pcaps/headers to the ticket.

max_engineer: Action plan: 1) gather origin logs for the trace id and timestamps; 2) reproduce with origin+edge; 3) check Fastly config for buffering proxies that may inject `Content-Length` or close connections early. Workarounds to test: set `cache-control: no-transform` on the origin response, and test disabling buffering in Fastly. Also try forcing chunked transfer on origin.

acme_prod: Will test bypass + Fastly config changes and upload pcaps to SUP-9831. Will report back here. Thanks! :pray:
